 4. Mr. M. A. Wallah Miah, learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the High Court Division upon a misconception of facts of the case wrongly held that the Writ Petition was filed alleging a breach of agreement or contract giving rise to a dispute which cannot be entertained in the Writ Jurisdiction. Mr. Wahab Miah submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate the case of the petitioners and wrongly dismissed the Writ. Petition on the ground of maintainability. 

 5. It is true that the High Court. Division suffered from a misconception of fact that there was already an agreement/contract between the parties and a dispute has arisen over the terms and conditions thereof which was the subject-matter of the Writ Petition. In fact the petitioners came to the Writ Court for a direction upon the respondents to finalise the agreement only on the basis of the recommendation of the Cabinet Committee as approved by the Prime Minister vide afore-said Memo dated 8.5.94. The High Court Division’s misconception was there but the misconceived nature of the petitioners' Writ Petition was equally showing. Unfortunately, the High Court Division failed to take notice of the same and proceeded upon a wrong ground of fact. The recommendation of a Cabinet Committee cannot be enforced through a Writ for the simple reason that it is not law. It is as simple as that The Writ Petition was misconceived at the inception.
